public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 421

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/421](https://www.erdosproblems.com/421)
- [Pratt26] K. Pratt, [A proof of Erdős Problem 421](https://www.erdosproblems.com/static/421-Pratt.pdf).
-/

@[expose] public section

open Set

namespace Erdos421

/--
There exists a sequence $1 \le d_1 < d_2 < \dots$ with density 1 such that all products
$\prod_{u \le i \le v} d_i$ are distinct. This was solved affirmatively; see [Pratt26]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos421.lean#L121"]
theorem erdos_421 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ (d : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono d ∧ 1 ≤ d 0 ∧ HasDensity (Set.range d) 1 ∧
    {(u, v) : ℕ × ℕ | u ≤ v}.InjOn fun (u, v) => ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc u v, d i := by
  sorry

end Erdos421

sources_consulted: K. Pratt, A “digested” proof of Erdős Problem #421, Theorem 1.1, Definition 1.2, and §7: https://www.erdosproblems.com/static/421-Pratt.pdf

review.notes: The sole declaration, Erdos421.erdos_421, faithfully states Pratt’s Theorem 1.1. StrictMono and the initial lower bound give an increasing sequence of positive integers; HasDensity is ordinary natural density; InjOn requires uniqueness of both endpoints for every nonempty consecutive block. Zero-based indexing and the density-counting endpoint convention are harmless. Scratch checks compiled successfully, including the explicit endpoint-uniqueness equivalence, finiteness of density-counting sets, the zero-denominator boundary, and exclusion of d 0 = 1 by injectivity. The affirmative answer and solved category agree with Pratt’s theorem. The linked formal theorem and its density definition match; a scan of its 541-module local import closure found no placeholders or custom axioms, although the external project was not rebuilt. The live problem page was blocked by Cloudflare despite descriptive User-Agent headers; the directly cited primary PDF supplied the statement and solution evidence.
